xDraft by xDev

Privacy Policy

Effective date: 12 October 2026

xDraft is built so that your maps and diagrams stay yours. This policy explains what the app, its App Clip and its Apple Watch app do with your data.

What we collect

Nothing. xDev does not run servers for xDraft, does not require an account, and does not include analytics, advertising or tracking. Your maps and diagrams are never sent to xDev.

Where your documents are stored

On your device. While you are signed in to iCloud, your mind maps, flowcharts, architecture and sequence diagrams (with their notes, images, sketches and chats) are also stored in your own private iCloud account, under Apple's privacy policy, so they appear on your other devices. Only you can read them there: xDev cannot read your iCloud data and receives nothing from it. To stop syncing, turn off iCloud Sync in xDraft ▸ Settings ▸ Data on a Mac, or turn off iCloud for xDraft in the Settings app on iPhone and iPad; your documents stay on the device.

AI features

AI features use Apple's on-device model (Apple Intelligence). xDraft 2.0.0 does not offer downloading any other AI model. Your text is processed on your device and is not sent to xDev. This covers every AI feature: Ask xDraft (including Translate), suggestions on topics, Suggest Fixes in Check Diagram, suggestions in architecture and sequence diagrams, and Draft with AI in the Architecture Document. Questions and answers in Ask About This Map, and questions typed in Ask xDraft that become a chat, are saved with the map they are about, stored and synced like the map, and deleted with it or with Clear Chat. Devices that cannot run Apple Intelligence do not show AI features.

Check Diagram and Architecture Document

Check Diagram looks for open ends in a diagram on your device; its findings are not saved. The Architecture Document and the Design Review Deck are built on your device from your architecture model. Their text stays in the window until you export it, and the PDF or Markdown file goes only where you save it.

Draw from a Folder

When you choose a folder for Draw from a Folder, xDraft reads the names of its files and subfolders (at most 150, three levels deep), never their contents, and skips hidden items. The names go to the on-device model to suggest a map. Access to the folder ends when the names are read; xDraft keeps no access for later, and the names are not stored unless you accept the map.

Sketches and Apple Pencil (iPad)

Sketches you draw with Apple Pencil are saved with the map. Sketch to Diagram and Convert to Topic read your strokes only when you tap Read Sketch or Convert to Topic: shapes and arrows are recognized by xDraft, handwriting by Apple's on-device recognition. Nothing is sent anywhere, and the result is only a suggestion until you make the flowchart or add the topic.

AI feedback

Thumbs-up and thumbs-down ratings stay on this device. Only the feature, rating and date are saved, never map content or prompts. Ratings are not synced or sent to xDev. Remove them with Clear AI Feedback in Settings ▸ Privacy.

Voice input

Speech is turned into text on your device and is not stored or sent to xDev. The app asks for microphone and speech recognition access the first time you use it.

Sharing into xDraft

Text, links, images and PDFs you share to xDraft from other apps are stored on your device until you add them to a map or discard them. Text in images and PDFs is recognized on your device.

AI apps you connect (Mac)

You can let AI apps on your Mac, such as Claude, Claude Code or ChatGPT, read your maps in xDraft ▸ Settings ▸ AI Apps. It is off until you turn it on, and each AI app has to be set up with the setup shown there. The AI app then starts a small helper inside xDraft that passes its requests to xDraft on your Mac; nothing goes over the network. A connected app can read the titles, notes and structure of your maps while xDraft is open, and may send what it reads to its own AI provider under that app's terms and privacy policy; check those before you connect it. xDraft does not send this data to xDev. If you also turn on Allow Suggestions, a connected app can propose new topics for a map; they appear labelled with the app's name and nothing is added until you accept them. Connected apps can't edit or delete anything in your maps. Turn the switch off to stop every app, or remove xDraft from one app's settings to stop that app.

Map links and the App Clip

Share Link turns a map, or one branch of it, into a link with the map inside it. The map is in the part of the link after `#`, which browsers do not send to any server, so xDev never receives it, not even when the link opens our web page; the page draws the map in your browser. The link goes only where you send it, and anyone who has it can read the map, as the app says before you share. On iPhone and iPad, a link can open in the xDraft App Clip without installing the app. The App Clip shows the map, can make a quick map with on-device AI, and keeps the last maps it opened or made (at most 10) in storage that only the xDraft app can read; if you install the app, it adds them to your library. Opening a link in the app adds a new map and changes nothing else.

Apple Watch

Ideas you add on Apple Watch go to your Inbox map, which is stored and synced through your private iCloud account like your other maps. To find that map on your devices, xDraft keeps its identifier (not its content) in iCloud key-value storage.

Spotlight and Shortcuts

Map titles are added to your device's own Spotlight index so you can find them; maps you delete are removed from it. Shortcuts actions run on your device.

Purchases

Payments are handled by Apple through the App Store. xDraft Pro subscriptions are billed, renewed and cancelled by Apple; you manage them in your App Store account settings. xDev does not receive your payment details.

Crash reports from Apple

If you choose to share analytics with app developers in your device settings, Apple may share crash reports and usage statistics with xDev. You control this in your device's privacy settings.

Deleting your data

Delete a map or diagram in the app to move it to Recently Deleted. It stays there for 30 days so you can restore it, then it is deleted permanently; Delete Permanently removes it straight away. Deleting the app removes the documents stored on that device. Documents in iCloud can be removed in your device's iCloud storage settings.

Children

The app does not collect data from anyone, including children.

Changes

If this policy changes, we update this page and the date above.
